clue.text: Any number in protests seen as fiends

indicators.note: the number is placed inside the word for protests

parts.note: demos are protest marches
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra

explanation.surface: Protest marches, whatever their size, are viewed as gatherings of devils.
explanation.definitionFit: Demons and fiends are both evil spirits, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Copper with sort of appeal in dynamic case

indicators.note: the copper and appeal pieces go inside the word for dynamic

parts.note: dynamic means active
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
SA is short for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A lively court case with a policeman and some sort of appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' and 'case' pull towards a police story; the case is grammatical.
explanation.definitionFit: The accusative is a grammatical case, the one marking a direct object.

clue.text: Cloth in which artist get wrapped up — it relieves the pain

indicators.note: the cloth is wrapped around the artist, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: lint is a soft fabric used for dressing wounds

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a British artist

explanation.surface: An artist is swaddled in cloth as a soothing remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Emin is a well-known British artist; her name is turned round and placed inside LINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Liniment is a rubbing lotion applied to ease aching muscles and joints.

clue.text: Heavenly sign holy saints placed outside church

parts.note: pi is a short informal word for pious, holy

indicators.note: the holy and saints pieces surround the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A sign in the sky, holy saints standing around a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisces is a constellation and a sign of the zodiac, the fishes.

clue.text: Doctor is apt, going round part of hospital, to see them?

definitions.text: Doctor is apt, going round part of hospital, to see them?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the hospital department
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A capable doctor goes round a hospital ward seeing people.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a doctor doing rounds sees these people.
explanation.definitionFit: Those a doctor visits on a ward round are the sick people under care.

clue.text: Transformed harpies about to become like angels

indicators.note: transformed letters are changed in form, rearranged

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Monstrous harpies are changed so that they become angelic.
explanation.walkthrough: Harpies are winged monsters of Greek myth, nicely set against angels.
explanation.definitionFit: Seraphs are an order of angels, so seraphic describes something angelic.

clue.text: Son wept going round gym — it's written down as a drama?

indicators.note: the word for wept surrounds the gym abbreviation

parts.note: wept means cried
PT is physical training, school gym

explanation.surface: A boy cried his way around the gym, a scene worthy of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A play's dialogue set down in a script has been put in written form beforehand.

clue.text: Come down heavily, when gathering of hunters is set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is written upwards

parts.note: a meet is an assembly of riders and hounds before a hunt

explanation.surface: Heavy rain falls just as the hunt is assembling.
explanation.definitionFit: Teem is used of rain pouring down hard, as in teeming with rain.

clue.text: Ruin in world below that's hot

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Destruction in a hellish underworld that is very hot.
explanation.definitionFit: To dish someone's hopes is an informal idiom for spoiling or wrecking them.

clue.text: Do this to get no person appearing alluring

definitions.meaning: spinning the little word on around, turning it, gives no

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is cryptic: turn ON and it reads NO.
explanation.definitionFit: An attractive, exciting person or thing is informally said to excite desire in someone.

clue.text: Company head goes by public transport, a north-south line

indicators.note: the headland is placed next to the other pieces

parts.note: a bus is public transport
the letter I is a single vertical stroke
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness

explanation.surface: A company boss travels by bus along a route running north to south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the company boss; it is a headland. The upright I is a north-south line.
explanation.definitionFit: A business is a commercial firm, synonymous with a company.

clue.text: Reason you finally departed — no longer having job leading

indicators.note: the first two pieces lead, coming before the rest

parts.note: ex means former
a post is a job

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word you

parts.note: late means dead, departed

explanation.surface: An argument that someone has gone, no longer heading their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reason' is a verb: to argue earnestly with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To expostulate is to remonstrate, arguing with someone to dissuade them.

clue.text: A foreign revolutionary steals a bit — it's not returned

parts.note: un is a in French

indicators.note: the revolutionary takes the other piece into itself

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary
quite means somewhat, a bit

explanation.surface: A foreign rebel pilfers something small that is never given back.
explanation.definitionFit: Love not reciprocated by the beloved is said to be unanswered.

clue.text: Dog in the role of pig or bird

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
as means in the capacity of
a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: An animal cast as either a pig or a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The curassow is a large turkey-like bird of tropical American forests.

clue.text: Curved instrument or tool that's cut off outside

indicators.note: the word for cut off goes outside the tool

parts.note: shorn means clipped, cut off
a hoe is a garden tool

explanation.surface: A curved implement or a tool that has been lopped off.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoehorn is a curved piece of horn or metal for easing the heel into a shoe.

clue.text: One attempting to keep male and maiden looking fitter?

indicators.note: the attempter holds the two letters inside

parts.note: a trier is one who tries
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Someone trying to keep a man and a girl looking in better shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Trimmer is the comparative of trim, slim and neat, so means in better condition.

clue.text: Dogs making row in church service

indicators.note: the row is placed inside the church service

parts.note: mass is a church service
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: Dogs causing a racket during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with cow here, meaning a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastiffs are large, powerful breeds of guard dog.

clue.text: One set of books introduces character in the other set, actually

indicators.note: the first pieces come before the character, leading it in

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
NT is the New Testament
Ruth is a figure and book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: One set of novels brings in a character from another series, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are adverbs asserting that something is really the case.

clue.text: Appropriate search before baddie comes into view

indicators.note: the search and baddie pieces go inside the word for view

parts.note: to view is to see

indicators.note: the search comes ahead of the baddie

parts.note: a quest is a search
a rat is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A fitting search ahead of a villain showing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' is the verb, to take possession of, not the adjective meaning fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: To sequestrate is to confiscate property legally, seizing it.

clue.text: Hard deposit of two salts

indicators.note: two calls for the sailor word to be given twice

parts.note: a tar or an old salt is a sailor

explanation.surface: A hard crust left behind by a pair of chemical salts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salts' suggests chemistry; old salts are sailors, each a TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartar is the hard calcified deposit that builds up on teeth.

clue.text: Group of players briefly playing at the Olympic Stadium

definitions.text: players briefly playing at the Olympic Stadium
definitions.meaning: West Ham United football club, shortened, whose ground is the former London Olympic Stadium

explanation.walkthrough: West Ham, a London football team, moved into the 2012 Olympic Stadium; W HAM is a short form of its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Wham! was a British pop duo of George Michael and Andrew Ridgeley.

clue.text: Music in endless traffic

indicators.note: endless drops the final letter of the word for traffic

parts.note: to traffic is to trade

explanation.surface: Music playing through traffic that never ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Trad is short for traditional jazz, a style of music.

clue.text: I met rich crook shunning company

indicators.note: crook as an adjective means bad or unwell, so the letters are put awry

explanation.surface: I encountered a wealthy villain who avoids people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like a criminal noun; it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit lives in solitude, so hermitic describes avoiding the society of others.

clue.text: Small island trader's end, squeezed by supermarket

indicators.note: the supermarket surrounds the single letter

parts.note: Tesco is a major British supermarket chain

indicators.note: the end of the word trader is its last letter

explanation.surface: A small trader on an island being crushed by a big supermarket.
explanation.walkthrough: Tresco is one of the Isles of Scilly off Cornwall; Tesco is Britain's largest supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tresco is the second largest of the Isles of Scilly, a small island.

clue.text: Reformer of church in church history, say

definitions.meaning: something that alters or changes things
in the phrase church history the first word qualifies the second, as a grammatical qualifier

explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformer' and 'church' suggest the Reformation, but the second sense is grammar: a noun qualifying another noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A modifier changes something, and in grammar is a word qualifying another word.

clue.text: Wander around town in Lancashire

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Strolling about a town in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire is a county in north-west England; Darwen is a town near Blackburn.
explanation.definitionFit: Darwen is a market town in Lancashire, an example of a place there.
